fairness.hero_subtitle: Pickket doesn't just say "we're fair." We automatically calculate fairness metrics for every allocation and transparently publish all results. Only verifiable fairness is real fairness.
fairness.principles_subtitle: Fairness guaranteed by structure, not words
fairness.p1_desc: 48-hour batch bidding, not first-come-first-served. Dawn queues, bot macros, and fast clicks mean nothing. Express your willingness to pay based on how much you truly want it.
fairness.p1_proof: Mileage allocation process ensures submission time has no effect on allocation results. Random closing makes sniping impossible.
fairness.p2_desc: Winners pay the displayed face value. This is a mathematical guarantee based on mileage allocation theory and Pickket's patented technology.
fairness.p2_proof: Mathematical proof: If winning condition w·b ≥ threshold, then payment m = threshold/w ≤ b always holds.
fairness.p3_desc: Overbidding offers no advantage, and underbidding only increases the risk of losing. The system makes honest bidding a dominant strategy (DSIC).
fairness.p3_proof: Fairness is mathematically guaranteed by mileage allocation theory. Pickket's patented technology applies this to ticket allocation. (Nobel Prize in Economics theory)
fairness.p4_desc: A fairness report is automatically generated after every allocation. Participation count, competition ratio, price distribution, Gini coefficient, and blocked fraudulent bids are all published.
fairness.p4_proof: Upon allocation completion, 5 fairness metrics are auto-calculated and displayed on the event detail page.
fairness.p5_desc: Fan weight acts only as a 'price discount.' Fans with higher weight purchase at lower prices, but allocation itself is value-based. New fans are actively accommodated.
fairness.p5_proof: 15% of all seats go to the new user lottery pool (Pool B), and 10% to the general lottery pool (Pool C).
fairness.cta_card_desc: Learn more about mileage allocation theory-based fair allocation, AP system, and the mathematical design behind it.
fairness.dashboard_title: This report is provided every time
fairness.dashboard_subtitle: Example of the fairness report automatically generated after every event allocation
fairness.before_1_text: First-come-first-served → Bots sell out in 0.3 seconds
fairness.before_4_text: Scalper prices 5~10x → Profits go to scalpers
fairness.after_3_text: Fees disclosed upfront → Verify before payment
fairness.after_4_text: 60% of surplus returned to ecosystem (Organizer 50% + Platform 10%)
fairness.after_5_text: +5% weight bonus for next session if rejected
fairness.stage_subtitle: 주최자가 조합하는 4단계 (최소 1개, 최대 4개). 미소화 좌석은 다음 단계로 자동 이월됩니다.
fairness.stage_1_desc: 유료 멤버십·팬클럽 회원 우선. 응모 기간(5~14일) 후 추첨. 최우선 좌석 블록, 1인 2매.
fairness.stage_2_desc: 전체 회원 대상. 7~14일 응모 후 AP 가중치 추첨. 0 AP로도 응모 가능, 투입 AP 소비됨.
fairness.stage_3_desc: 오픈 시간 접속 후 랜덤 순번 배정. 순서대로 좌석 선택 + 결제. AP는 수수료 할인에만 사용.
fairness.stage_4_desc: 이전 단계 잔여석만 판매. 항상 마지막 단계. 캡챠 + 1인 2매 + 1계정-1기기 제한.
fairness.anti_subtitle: Prevention, not punishment. The system automatically detects and blocks fraud.
fairness.anti_bot_1: Mileage allocation process: Submission time has no effect on results
fairness.anti_bot_2: Random closing: Exact end time is unpredictable
fairness.anti_bot_3: Behavior analysis: Automated patterns detected in real-time
fairness.anti_multi_1: Auto-flag for 3+ accounts on the same IP
fairness.anti_multi_2: Cluster analysis for consecutive bids within 2 seconds
fairness.anti_multi_3: Shared payment method group detection (40% weight)
fairness.anti_overbid_1: Based on mileage allocation theory: System manipulation impossible (mathematically proven)
fairness.anti_overbid_3: Bid modification locked 60 minutes before closing
fairness.anti_scalp_1: PASS real-name verification required (anti-scalping law compliant)
fairness.verify_subtitle: Anyone can independently verify lottery results using the Commit-Reveal scheme
fairness.verify_step1_desc: Before the lottery, the server seed's hash (SHA-256) is recorded on the blockchain. This hash cannot be changed after the lottery.
fairness.verify_step2_desc: After the lottery, the server seed is published. The final seed, combined with the participant seed, determines the lottery result.

fairness.tp_trust_desc: Mathematical proof (mileage allocation theory's mathematical guarantees) + External media verification (independent press joint analysis) + Public data (concert index & impact report regular publication). We build structural trust, not self-claims.
fairness.faq_1_q: Is it really impossible to pay more than my bid?
fairness.faq_1_a: Absolutely not. Mileage allocation theory and Pickket's patented technology mathematically guarantee face-value payment upon winning.
fairness.faq_2_q: Does a high fan weight guarantee winning?
fairness.faq_2_a: No. Weight only affects 'price.' Allocation is determined by weighted value (w × b), so even with low weight, you can win by bidding high enough. Also, 25% of all seats are allocated via lottery pools (B+C), giving everyone a chance.
fairness.faq_3_q: How do I interpret the fairness index (Gini coefficient)?
fairness.faq_3_a: Closer to 0 means all winners paid similar prices; closer to 1 means larger gaps. Pickket displays (1 - Gini) as the "Fairness Index," so 0.9 or above is rated "Very Fair."
fairness.faq_4_q: Am I penalized next time if I lose this round?
fairness.faq_4_a: Quite the opposite. A rejection bonus (+5% per round) is added to your weight for the same artist's next session (tour). The more consecutive rejections, the better your chances next time.
fairness.faq_5_q: Can I set any resale price I want?
fairness.faq_5_a: There's no price cap, but the structure where 60% of surplus goes back to the ecosystem (organizer 50%, platform 10%) naturally suppresses prices (soft cap). Sellers keep only 40% of the surplus, greatly reducing the incentive for excessive pricing. Face-value transfers have zero fees.

blog.hero_description: Pickket's RISE engine is built on point-weighted lotteries. From lottery design to fan weights and fairness metrics — we share our technology philosophy.
blog.lottery_title: AP Fair Allocation: Fair Distribution Prioritizing Real Fans
blog.lottery_subtitle: AP fair allocation reflects fan activity points in distribution priority, creating a structure that favors genuine fans.
blog.lottery_section1_p1: Traditional first-come-first-served systems reward speed. Bots and macros have the advantage. AP fair allocation, on the other hand, rewards fan activity and loyalty. Fans who have consistently supported an artist receive higher allocation priority, and the system executes fair and transparent distribution.
blog.lottery_section2_p1: Pickket combines two types of points to calculate winning probability:
blog.lottery_lp_desc: Points accumulated through fan activities like fan club membership, music streaming, and concert attendance. Permanent tier points that persist even after use.
blog.lottery_ap_desc: Points consumed when applying. More AP invested means higher winning probability, with partial refunds on losing.
blog.lottery_section3_p1: When N applicants compete for K seats, each applicant's winning probability is:
blog.lottery_wi_desc: Fan loyalty-based weight derived from LP (0.5–2.0)
blog.lottery_api_desc: Action points the applicant invested in this event
blog.lottery_guarantee1_desc: Higher winning probability for genuine fans. Loyalty becomes competitive advantage in a fair structure.
blog.lottery_guarantee2_desc: New fans are guaranteed a base probability. Anyone can apply without points and everyone has a chance to win.
blog.lottery_guarantee3_desc: The lottery process and probability calculations are fully open. Based on verifiable random function (VRF).
blog.lottery_proof_line1: Fair allocation probability: Pᵢ = (wᵢ · APᵢ) / Total
blog.lottery_proof_line2: Minimum guarantee: base_prob ≥ 0.01 for all applicants
blog.lottery_proof_line3: ∴ Even new fans with 0 points are guaranteed at least 1% winning probability ✓
blog.fan_weight_title: 5-Dimensional Fan Weight: How We Measure Real Fans
blog.fan_weight_subtitle: Pickket quantifies fan loyalty across 5 axes. Weights directly affect lottery winning probability, enabling genuine fan-first distribution.
blog.fan_weight_dim1_desc: Fan club membership duration, music streaming, SNS follows
blog.fan_weight_dim2_desc: Attendance count with 2-year half-life exponential decay
blog.fan_weight_dim5_desc: Activity within last 180 days (consideration for new fans)
blog.fan_weight_section2_p1: After weighted summation of 5 scores, normalized with a sigmoid function:
blog.fan_weight_linear_desc: Extreme values dominate weights. A perfect score in one dimension can make the rest meaningless.
blog.fan_weight_sigmoid_desc: Sensitive in the center, gradual at extremes. Naturally suppresses outlier influence.
blog.fan_weight_range_desc: Up to 3.38x difference in winning probability is possible, but this is framed as "Fan Recognition". High-weight fans receive higher winning probabilities, while low-weight fans receive probabilities closer to the base rate.
blog.batch_title: Batch Entry: Eliminating Speed Competition by Design
blog.batch_subtitle: 24–72 hour application windows with random deadlines structurally neutralize bots and sniping.
blog.batch_section2_p1: Nobody knows the exact closing time. The deadline is randomized within 0–30 minutes after the scheduled time. Last-moment sniping strategies are structurally impossible.
blog.batch_section3_p1: Instead of discrete levels ("normal/high/very high"), we use a continuous sigmoid. Why? Because crossing a discrete boundary triggers information cascades (Banerjee, 1992), causing herd behavior.
blog.fairness_title: Fairness Metrics: Proving Every Distribution with Numbers
blog.fairness_subtitle: Pickket automatically calculates 5 fairness metrics per distribution and provides transparency reports.
blog.fairness_metric1_desc: Actual winning ratio vs. point weights. Closer to 1 means fairer results.
blog.fairness_metric2_desc: Correlation between loyalty point rank and winning rate. Higher means better genuine fan prioritization.
blog.fairness_metric3_desc: Evenness of winning probability distribution. Closer to 0 is more equal, closer to 1 is more unequal.
blog.fairness_metric4_desc: >1 indicates systematic over-application. Should converge to 1 in lotteries.
blog.fairness_metric5_desc: Positive is normal (high weight → high win rate). Negative signals a system anomaly.
blog.fairness_metric6_desc: Measures scalping incentive. Dividing by w² quadratically dampens risk for genuine fans.
blog.fairness_winner_item4: "Your fan activity increased your winning probability by X%"
blog.fairness_loser_item3: "Join the fan club to increase your chances next time"
blog.resale_title: Resale Profit Recapture Model: Returning Scalper Profits to the Ecosystem
blog.resale_subtitle: Pickket's resale system structurally suppresses scalping incentives through a profit recapture model, returning profits to artists and the fan ecosystem.
blog.resale_platform_desc: 10% of profit · Trade brokerage and escrow
blog.resale_math_note: premium = max(0, resale_price - original_price) · 60% of profit returns to ecosystem
blog.resale_section2_p1: Instead of a hard cap, 60% of profit is returned to the organizer (50%) and platform (10%). Sellers only keep 40% of profit, structurally suppressing scalping incentives. Face-value transfers incur zero fees. Recaptured profits are reinvested in artist and fan ecosystem development.
blog.resale_orderbook1_desc: Price registered by seller. Sorted by lowest price.
blog.resale_orderbook2_desc: Maximum price offered by buyer. Sorted by highest price.
blog.resale_orderbook3_desc: Executed via Redis distributed lock when lowest ask ≤ highest bid.
blog.concert_index_title: K-POP Concert Index: Toward a Bloomberg for Entertainment
blog.concert_index_subtitle: Pickket systematically collects and analyzes concert market price data to publish the K-POP Concert Index.
blog.concert_index_section1_p1: The stock market has KOSPI, real estate has the KB Index. But the multi-trillion-won concert market has no price indicator. Pickket builds the concert market's first systematic price index, based on real demand and transaction data accumulated through AP fair allocation and resale data.
blog.concert_index_tpi_desc: Weighted average transaction price by tier. Measures artist popularity and market overheating through time series.
blog.concert_index_cdi_desc: Combination of application-to-seat ratio and competition sigmoid. Quantifies demand pressure.
blog.concert_index_fsi_desc: Product of consumer surplus ratio and price equality. Higher means greater perceived fairness.
blog.concert_index_rhi_desc: Inverse indicator of resale risk score and price premium. Closer to 1 means healthier secondary market.
blog.concert_index_dashboard_title: Concept Demo: K-POP Concert Index Dashboard
blog.concert_index_dashboard_desc: A prototype calculated from actual Pickket event data. Will be updated in real-time at official launch.
blog.concert_index_tpi_chart_note: Based on weighted avg. transaction price
blog.concert_index_fsi_formula_note: FSI = Surplus Ratio × (1-Gini). Closer to 1 = more satisfied
blog.concert_index_rhi_formula_note: RHI = 1 - Resale Risk × Premium. Most maintain 0.8+ with 60% profit recapture
blog.concert_index_dashboard_footer_data: Data: Based on Pickket lottery & resale transaction prices · De-identified statistics
blog.concert_index_usage1: Determine tour scale & pricing with TPI trends
blog.concert_index_usage3: Monitor market health with FSI & RHI
blog.concert_index_usage4: Measure policy effectiveness with resale price trends
blog.concert_index_principle1_desc: Based on lottery allocation and resale transaction prices. Actual demand and trading prices

blog.compliance_subtitle: Pickket technically complies with the 2026 Anti-Scalping Three Laws, E-Commerce Act, and Performance Act.
blog.compliance_pool_order: Allocation order: A → D → B → C. Sequential allocation starting from the highest verification pool.

purchase.q1: How is Pickket's fair distribution different?
purchase.a1: Pickket uses a lottery system powered by a fair distribution engine. Unlike first-come-first-served (which favors bots), tickets are allocated at face value to genuine fans who commit AP.
purchase.q2: How many tickets can I purchase at most?
purchase.a2: You can purchase up to 4 tickets per person. Limits may vary by event — please check each event's detail page.
purchase.a3: AP has two uses. ① Lottery weight: the more AP you commit, the higher your winning odds (committed AP is consumed). ② Booking fee discount: get up to 70% off (₩1,400) on the ₩2,000 booking fee. Earn AP by attending shows, writing reviews, and participating in the community.

payment.a1: We support credit/debit cards, Kakao Pay, Naver Pay, Toss Pay, and bank transfer. All payments are processed securely through PortOne.
payment.q2: How do I request a refund?
payment.a2: You may cancel within 7 days of purchase and up to 10 days before the event. Refunds are processed to the original payment method within 3–5 business days. Please contact support@pickket.kr.
payment.a3: No, all prices are VAT-inclusive. There are no additional taxes.

resale.a1: 50% of the resale markup (sale price − face value) goes to the organizer (artist/producer), and 10% to the platform. The seller receives 100% of face value plus 40% of the markup. No fee applies for face-value transfers.
resale.q2: Is there a cap on resale prices?
resale.a2: There is no hard cap. Instead, 60% of the markup (50% organizer + 10% platform) is returned to the ecosystem, creating a natural price-dampening effect. Organizers can set a per-event ceiling if they choose.
resale.q3: Are there fees for buying a resale ticket?
resale.a3: No extra fees for buyers. The ₩2,000 booking fee is pre-included in the listed price (all-in pricing). For resales, fees are deducted only from the seller's markup (50% organizer + 10% platform). Face-value transfers are fee-free.

row1.limit: System paralyzed by server overload. Opaque selection criteria. A U.S. Senate hearing was held.

row2.attempt: App-only sales + no transfer + automatic resale to waitlist if unable to attend.
row2.limit: Focused on small venues. Limited scalability for large events and global scale.

row3.attempt: Mobile-only tickets + ID verification + capped-price resale market.
row3.limit: Dependent on exclusive venue contracts. Consumer platform choice is restricted.
